questions.q: What does “2207” mean in a motor designation?
questions.explain: The first two digits are the stator diameter in mm, the second two the height. A bigger stator means more torque.

questions.q: A 1750KV motor on 6S (25.2 V) with no load spins at roughly…
questions.explain: KV is RPM per volt with no load: 1750 × 25.2 ≈ 44,000 rpm. Less with a prop on.

questions.q: Why is DShot better than PWM?
options: It's analog, so it's more precise
A digital frame with a CRC
questions.explain: No range calibration needed, and noise doesn't shift the throttle.

questions.q: What does the ESC send back over bidirectional DShot?
questions.explain: The DShot return channel carries electrical RPM. The RPM filter is built on this.
In June 2024 BLHeli_32 shut down. Existing ESCs work, but there are no updates. The replacement for 32-bit ESCs is AM32, for BLHeli_S it's Bluejay.

options: The ESC lost the rotor position
The ESC frequency out of sync with the radio
questions.explain: Sensorless control determines the rotor position from the back-EMF. On a sharp load change the estimate breaks down — the motor loses sync.

questions.q: How do you get shaft RPM from eRPM?
questions.explain: Electrical RPM is divided by the number of pole pairs: for 14 magnets, by 7.

questions.q: The Kt of a 1750KV motor is roughly:
How many bits of throttle value are in a DShot frame, and what is the range?
questions.explain: 0 — stop, 1–47 — commands; plus a telemetry bit and 4 CRC bits.
